plan.authors: Laurens van der Maaten   ·   Geoffrey Hinton
plan.publication: Journal of Machine Learning Research   /   Vol. 9   /   2008
plan.question: Which neighbors stay together when 784 pixel values become two coordinates?
plan.method: t-SNE turns pixel-space distances into neighbor probabilities. It moves points in the map to preserve likely neighbors. A heavy-tailed Student distribution gives less similar points room to spread out.
plan.method_caption: The three gradient fields show how the force on a pair changes with its distance in the input and in the map.
plan.main_caption: Each color denotes a digit class. t-SNE (top) separates many classes that overlap in the Sammon map (bottom). Both plots use the same samples.
plan.secondary_caption: Paths through unselected observations help estimate how strongly landmarks A, B and C should be linked.
plan.detail: Random walks on all 60,000 MNIST images placed 6,000 landmarks. In ten-fold cross-validation, the same classifier had 5.75% error in the original 784 dimensions.
plan.limitation: Different runs can settle on different maps. The authors also caution that high intrinsic dimensionality can make local neighborhoods unreliable.
